decisions.reason: The candidate already has a complete same-message MODIFY recording the uppercase supporting V, conditional later case exploration, and all-caps wordmark scope; no additional or corrected Event is needed.
Applying an all-caps treatment to the complete VEILLVÉ wordmark necessarily establishes uppercase treatment for the internal proprietary letterforms, and the candidate has no matching Event.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Kenji,

Before work begins, I want to clarify the direction for the first complete VEILLVÉ wordmark: please continue initially with the all-caps treatment. My instinct is that all caps is the right first direction because of the architectural rhythm it creates, particularly with the hero V leading the word.

Another case treatment can certainly be explored if, after we have reviewed the complete wordmark, a compelling reason appears. Until then, it is important to see the architectural vision we have spent months developing come together as one complete identity.

That treatment emerged naturally during the process while the hero V was being developed; I realized, however, that I had never made a conscious decision about it. We have now established the architectural language, and applying it to the complete wordmark is exactly where I hoped we would go next. I am excited to see the system functioning as a whole.

I am really looking forward to the first VEILLVÉ wordmark.

value_updates.case_treatment: Use uppercase internal letterforms in the initial complete VEILLVÉ wordmark; explore another case treatment only if later review provides a compelling reason.

decisions.reason: The Hero V is already explicitly a capital opening V with approved geometry; selecting an all-caps treatment for the complete wordmark does not alter that geometry or its existing role.
The all-caps composition decision implements the established architectural identity but does not change the candidate's broader brand-purpose, tone, positioning, or expression requirements.
The source uses 'treatment' to mean letter case and makes no decision about champagne-gold material, finish, sequencing, or the candidate's deferred lifecycle.
The all-caps decision does not change how the É accent is derived or copied from the approved Hero V terminal; the candidate's existing derivation rule remains valid unchanged.
Letter-case selection for the complete wordmark does not modify the shared terminal geometry, constraints, expression, or application across the V system.
Choosing all caps for the initial complete wordmark does not change the requirement that the identity remain wordmark-led without a separate icon or monogram.
